title: Dynamic changes in plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease in patients treated with lecanemab: a longitudinal cohort study
title_zh: Lecanemab治疗患者血浆阿尔茨海默病生物标志物的动态变化：一项纵向队列研究
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-amyloid antibodies slow cognitive and functional decline in individuals with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, but few studies have examined changes associated with these treatments in plasma biomarkers linked to neurodegeneration. We analysed changes in a panel of 130 plasma proteins and their associations with conversion to amyloid PET negative status and cognitive changes in patients receiving lecanemab infusions as part of their clinical care. METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study included patients with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease and positive amyloid biomarkers who were identified as candidates for biweekly lecanemab infusions based on the US Food and Drug Administration label and consented to blood collection at the Washington University Memory Diagnostic Center (St Louis, MO, USA) between July 17, 2023, and Oct 10, 2025. Lecanemab was administered as a 10 mg/kg intravenous infusion every 2 weeks. Patients underwent clinical assessments and blood draws approximately every 6 months over up to 2 years. Research participants enrolled at the Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight ADRC; St Louis, MO, USA) between May 3, 1996, and Feb 27, 2025, and who did not receive anti-amyloid antibodies, were included as control groups (an amyloid β-negative [Aβ-] group without cognitive impairment and an untreated group with cognitive impairment). The primary outcome was change in plasma concentrations of protein biomarkers associated with Alzheimer's disease pathology with lecanemab treatment. Associations between plasma biomarker changes and number of lecanemab infusions were examined using regression and mixed-effects models, with adjustment for demographics. FINDINGS: The study included 197 patients in whom lecanemab infusions had been started (lecanemab group), as well as 173 patients in whom lecanemab had been ordered but not yet started, who were combined with 1139 research participants with cognitive impairment from the Knight ADRC cohort to form the untreated control group with cognitive impairment (n=1312). An additional 458 research participants formed the Aβ- control group without cognitive impairment. In the lecanemab group, the median patient age was 73 years (IQR 69-77); 104 (53%) were female and 93 (47%) were male; and most participants were White (187 [98%] of 190 with available data) and non-Hispanic (183 [97%] of 188 with available data). 130 biomarkers were classified into four distinct trajectories, with 34 showing significant changes (false discovery rate <0·05) in the lecanemab group. The trajectories were: normalising, with biomarkers shifting towards concentrations found in Aβ-individuals without cognitive impairment (eg, phosphorylated tau [p-tau]217, MAPT, and GFAP); overcorrecting, with biomarkers shifting towards and then beyond concentrations found in Aβ- individuals without cognitive impairment (eg, amyloid β peptides); opposite, with biomarkers shifting further from concentrations found in Aβ- individuals without cognitive impairment (eg, NPTXR, NRGN, and TREM2); and unchanged (eg, NEFL and APOE). INTERPRETATION: Lecanemab treatment was associated with dynamic, multidirectional changes across plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease pathology, with partial normalisation of amyloid and tau biomarkers alongside abnormal concentrations of inflammatory and neurodegeneration-related biomarkers (eg, TREM2 and NPTXR), which might reflect an immune response to amyloid plaques and effects of treatment on neuronal and synaptic processes distinct from amyloid clearance. These divergent trajectories suggest that different biomarkers could eventually serve different clinical purposes, such as monitoring treatment response or informing patient prognosis, although further validation is needed. FUNDING: National Institute on Aging, Cure Alzheimer's Fund, and Washington University.
abstract_zh: 背景：抗淀粉样抗体可减缓早期症状性阿尔茨海默病患者的认知和功能衰退，但很少有研究探讨这些治疗相关的血浆生物标志物变化。我们分析了130种血浆蛋白的变化及其与淀粉样PET阴性状态转变和认知变化的关联，研究对象为接受Lecanemab输注的患者。方法：本纵向队列研究纳入早期症状性阿尔茨海默病且淀粉样生物标志物阳性的患者，这些患者根据美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）标签被认定为每两周一次Lecanemab输注的候选者，并在2023年7月17日至2025年10月10日期间在华盛顿大学记忆诊断中心（密苏里州圣路易斯）同意采血。Lecanemab以10 mg/kg静脉输注，每两周一次。患者在最多两年内每约六个月接受临床评估和血样采集。未接受抗淀粉样抗体的研究参与者（来自Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center，密苏里州圣路易斯，1996年5月3日至2025年2月27日）被纳入对照组，包括无认知障碍的淀粉样β阴性（Aβ-）组和未治疗的认知障碍组。主要结局是Lecanemab治疗期间血浆蛋白生物标志物浓度的变化。使用回归和混合效应模型，并调整人口统计学变量，检验血浆生物标志物变化与Lecanemab输注次数的关联。结果：研究共纳入197名已开始Lecanemab输注的患者（Lecanemab组），以及173名已下单但尚未开始输注的患者，这些患者与Knight ADRC队列中1139名认知障碍研究参与者合并，形成未治疗的认知障碍对照组（n=1312）。另外458名研究参与者构成无认知障碍的Aβ-对照组。Lecanemab组中，中位年龄73岁（四分位距69-77岁）；女性104人（53%），男性93人（47%）；大多数为白人（190人中187人，98%）且非西班牙裔（188人中183人，97%）。130种生物标志物被分为四条不同轨迹，其中34种在Lecanemab组中显示显著变化（假发现率<0.05）。轨迹包括：趋于正常化（如磷酸化tau [p-tau]217、MAPT和GFAP），过度校正（如淀粉样β肽），相反方向（如NPTXR、NRGN和TREM2），以及不变（如NEFL和APOE）。解释：Lecanemab治疗与阿尔茨海默病病理相关血浆生物标志物的多向动态变化相关，部分淀粉样和tau生物标志物趋于正常化，同时炎症和神经退行性相关生物标志物（如TREM2和NPTXR）出现异常浓度，可能反映对淀粉样斑块的免疫反应以及治疗对神经元和突触过程的影响，独立于淀粉样清除。不同轨迹表明不同生物标志物未来可能用于不同临床目的，如监测治疗反应或预测患者预后，但仍需进一步验证。资助：美国国立老龄研究所、Cure Alzheimer's基金会和华盛顿大学。
